title: Signal throttle and metric loss — on-call investigation + tuning notes
content:
TL;DR: During a noisy week of SLO burn alerts we observed spuriously rising error-rate metrics coming from an internal inference router exporter. Root cause was a combination of exporter backpressure under intermittent GC stalls and a recent Alertmanager suppression policy that aggressively reopens grouped alerts. Result: flapping SLO alerts + oncall fatigue. These notes capture the timeline, investigative commands, short-term mitigations, and longer-term runbook/tuning changes we should adopt.

1) Incident summary (informal)
- Symptoms: frequent SLO burn alerts for /generate endpoints (p50/p95 latency + error rate) between 2025-11-01 and 2025-11-03. Alerts repeatedly opened/closed every ~15–40m. Oncall pagers saturated for multiple teams.
- Observed at first glance: Prometheus scrape errors and high pushgateway queue in the inference-router-exporter. Metrics for router error_count spiked in lockstep with scrape failures.
- Initial mitigation: temporarily increased alert thresholds and enabled a 30m coherence window in Alertmanager for the affected group to avoid flapping.

2) Chronological notes (investigation snippets)
- 2025-11-03 02:14 PST: pager page triggered (SLO burn for generate-route).
- 02:18: check prom targets: prometheus > Status > Targets showed inference-router-exporter 503s with 500ms+ response times.
- 02:21: ssh to exporter pod (k8s: inference-router-exporter-77ff) and kubectl logs: saw periodic GC pause/logging in JVM (we run a thin java shim for metrics).
- 02:26: curl /metrics endpoint locally — response time varied widely (20ms -> 800ms) depending on sampling.
- 02:33: Prometheus scrape latency metric (prometheus_target_interval_length_seconds) correlated with error_count spikes.
- 02:45: Confirmed Alertmanager groups were reopening because silence window had many individual alert instances that expired and re-fired; suppression policy allowed reopen.

3) Key findings / root cause chain (hypothesis consolidated)
- Inference router's metrics shim experiences intermittent GC/backpressure which causes the /metrics endpoint to slow or intermittently error.
- Prometheus treats partial failures as missing samples and some rate rules compute artificially high error rates when scraped sparsely (division by near-zero scrape counts in rate calculations).
- Alert rules we have for SLO burn use short evaluation windows (5m) and do not guard against low-scrape scenarios -> leads to transient spikes being treated as real.
- Alertmanager grouping/suppression configuration has a low aggregation_coherence and no minimum firing duration; when exporter recovers briefly, alerts close then reopen as next scrape fails.

4) Repro steps and investigation commands (copyable)
- Check scrape target health:
  - curl -sS 'http://prometheus.example.internal/api/v1/targets' | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.scrapeUrl|contains("inference-router-exporter"))'
- Inspect rate rule that triggered SLO burn (example rule):
  - cat /etc/prometheus/rules/slo_rules.yml | sed -n '/generate-error-rate/,/\$/p'
- Local reproduce of missing-sample artifact:
  - Use prometheus-query: 'avg_over_time(increase(router_errors_total[5m])[5m:1m]) / increase(router_requests_total[5m])' to see division by near-zero artifacts.
- Pod investigation:
  - kubectl -n infra exec -it <exporter-pod> -- jcmd GC.heap_info (or check container logs for GC pause markers)

5) Short-term mitigations applied (what we did during oncall)
- Increased alert rule evaluation window for the problematic SLO alert from 5m to 15m (hotfix) to require sustained signal.
- Added 'min_samples' guard in PromQL expression: 'unless (increase(router_requests_total[15m]) < 5)' to avoid firing on low-scrape windows.
- Temporarily increased Alertmanager group_wait/group_interval to 30m for the SLO group to avoid reopen noise while root cause addressed.
- Restarted exporter autoscaler to rotate pods; applied a JVM flag tweak (turned on G1 periodic pause avoidance flags) as trial.

6) Runbook/runbook-draft edits to add (concrete changes to store in repo)
- New subsection: 'Handling intermittent scraper-originated SLO spikes' with steps:
  - Check prometheus scrape latency and target health (link to query).
  - Confirm whether the alerting expression includes minimum sample count or min_requests guard.
  - If missing-sample artifact suspected, backdate query with longer window (30m) to verify persistence.
  - If exporter is overloaded/GCing, scale or restart the exporter and mark the target for follow-up.
- Include sample PromQL snippets to always include 'and (increase(router_requests_total[15m]) > 3)'.
- Add a prescriptive Alertmanager rule: 'do not reopen group if the same fingerprint repopulated within threshold X unless ephemeral_count > Y'. (Implementation note: file a follow-up to implement via templated inhibition or use external silence enforcement)

7) Tuning recommendations (medium/long-term)
- Prometheus/alerts:
  - Prefer 15–30m evaluation windows for SLO burn alerts; keep short windows only for rapid incident detection alerts with explicit low-sample handling.
  - Add sample-count guards to all rate-based SLO rules where denominator can be zero or near-zero.
  - Replace fragile rate() uses with increase() + clamp_by_samples when appropriate.
- Exporters:
  - Replace java-based thin shim with a Go exporter or instrumented servlet that is non-blocking for metrics collection.
  - Add read-only /health and /metrics endpoints separated so scrape load can't trigger heavy code paths.
- Alertmanager:
  - Add 'minimum firing duration' metadata (or silence enforcement) for groups that historically re-open.
  - Review grouping labels to ensure stable grouping of alerts from the same root cause (reduce over-splitting by hostname if not necessary).
- Observability platform:
  - Add a 'scrape-availability' dashboard and a daily alert that detects targets with >10% missing scrapes in last 24h.
  - Instrument exporter with a fast metric that reports 'exporter busy' when internal queue length > N.

8) Post-incident action items (owners + dates)
- (Evan Chen) Replace exporter shim with non-blocking Go implementation — prototype by 2026-03-15, rollout plan by 2026-04-12.
- (Mariana Ortiz) Add min-sample guards to all SLO rules across shared prometheus repo — PR by 2026-02-14 (PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/874).
- (Samir Kapoor) Implement Alertmanager inhibition policy for reopen suppression and minimum firing duration — design doc by 2026-03-01.
- (Lina Tran) Create scrape-availability dashboard and alert (grafana board + playbook link) — complete by 2026-02-28.
- (Oncall rotation) Add a quick checklist to oncall handoff notes: 1) check scrape health, 2) check exporter GC/CPU before treating SLO spike as prod issue.

9) Open questions (we couldn't fully answer during incident)
- Is the rate rule math robust enough for all router endpoints with low volume tenants? We need to audit low-volume routes separately.
- Do we want a global guard that silences SLO burn alerts if more than X% of scrape targets are missing (indicating platform scraper problem)?
- How to instrument exporter so metric emission never blocks app threads (reporting options and language tradeoffs).

10) Notes for future runbook examples (copy/paste friendly)
- PromQL example to avoid division-by-zero artifacts:
  - (increase(router_errors_total[15m]) / clamp_min(increase(router_requests_total[15m]), 1)) unless increase(router_requests_total[15m]) < 3
- Alertmanager sample config snippet (conceptual):
  - group_wait: 30m
  - group_interval: 30m
  - repeat_interval: 4h
  - ...plus 'min_firing_duration' custom label enforcement via our orchestration layer.

Appendix (raw snippets / logs we captured)
- exporter logs sample: '2025-11-03T02:22:10Z [main] INFO GC pause 1234ms; metrics-thread blocked'
- Prometheus target sample output: 'lastScrapeDuration: 0.82, lastScrapeStatus: error'
- Alert rule that fired (before change): 'expr: (sum(rate(router_errors_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(router_requests_total[5m])) by (route)) > 0.05'

Final note: this doc is intentionally informal. Goal is to capture enough context so infra-config and alerting teams can make pragmatic changes without losing the oncall intuition. Please add comments inline or open followups using JIRA-OPS-4127.

-- Evan
